title: phase 4b people build A, two players: (train) the client trains one of the host's employees - routed, the host's machine pays once and runs the game's own training; (transfer) the client moves a second host employee to a client shop (release on the host, adopt on the client) and back again; (candidates) the client claims one of the host's candidates and the host, its owner, is refused while the claim stands; the pool is listed on both machines; ends dissolved
preconditions: Fixture save1. Build A deployed. The host's staff at its first flipped shop are injected copies on the client (T-P0/T-P4-BONUS precedent). The transfer round trip returns the employee to the host's shop with the same id but leaves them unscheduled (the release unassigns shifts) - a fixture mutation, recorded. Candidate counts depend on the fixture and are reported, not asserted. Ends dissolved.

steps.note: host view: the client's first flipped building = the transfer destination
the client's world needs to settle; the host's staff copies land on the client
client view: the host's first flipped building

two DIFFERENT injected copies of the host's staff (BAMP_DUTY synthetics skipped): empTrain = the first with a primary skill below 100 (run 6: a maxed employee prices training at 0); empMove = the LAST injected row (run 7: the second row was the same employee as empTrain, and the game's own training unassigns them - assignedAddress null - so the host rightly refused the move 'they are at ''' (owner wins))
P3 TRAIN: nothing charged on the client; the host's machine re-runs the game's own training sequence once (its own price) on the real record

\[Transfer\] .*: ADOPTED by '${clientPid}' at '${clientShop}' - one save holds the record again

the host's in-transit table is empty after the ack
the moved employee is now the CLIENT's own record at the client shop (same id, injected=False)

\[Transfer\] .*: ADOPTED by '${hostPid}' at '${hostShop}' - one save holds the record again

back home as the HOST's own record, same id
P1 POOL (reported): the host's own candidates (origin=mine) + the client's copies

the client's view of the host's pool; the first candidate NOBODY holds (run 8: the client's fixture save now carries a live negotiation for Jose King, opened by run 5's rig claim and saved by the coordinated save, so the client re-asserts that claim at connect and it is granted before this leg runs)
P1 CLAIM: the client asks first and is granted; 'hold' keeps a synthetic live negotiation so the 5 s sweep does not release it
